full_judgment: 9. Mr. S S. Halder, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant agreeing with the proposition that possession of a co-sharer would not amount to dispossession of another co-sharer, urged that in case of ouster the co-sharer dispossessed would be required to ask a relief for khan possession which having not been asked for in the instant suit, the suit was not maintainable I found no substance in this contention also A co-sharer is not dispossessed only because he was kept out of possession as the possession of one co-sharer would be the possession for all. But that does not mean that a co-sharer could never acquire a title by adverse possession by ousting the other co-sharer and thereby dispossessing him from his possession An ouster to amount to dispossession of another co-sharer must be hostile, notorious by claiming a sole title to the exclusion of the dispossessed co-sharer and only in a case of such an ouster, founded upon facts, a co-sharer plaintiff, in a partition suit out of possession would be required to ask for possession after payment of ad valorem court fees of the value of the suit property claimed in his share. But that is not the case here as there is nothing on record to show that there in fact existed as ouster so to compel the plaintiff to make a prayer for possession after payment of ad valorem court feces. Further non-payment of court fees or less payment of court fees would be a mere irregularity and shall not by itself entail a reversal or variation of the decree of the court below. In the view I have taken herein before I am supported by a number of decisions of Indian Jurisdiction and I would remain content by referring only to a few. In the case of Bidhata Rai Vs.
